title: What Do You Like?
description: Ask about and state food preferences.
objectives: Ask about and state food preferences.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to ask about and state food preferences. The central language is like, don't like, and preference questions. It belongs to the practical context of food & café english. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: like, don't like, and preference questions

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the what do you like? exchange.

blocks.english: I like tea, but I don't like coffee.
blocks.explanation: This what do you like? model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the what do you like? exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “What food do you like?” and “I like tea, but I don't like coffee.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: like, don't like, and preference questions.
